items.briefing:
Australians are being urged to stay alert to two active scam threats: Proofpoint has identified myGov impersonation scams and fake invoice emails targeting people in Australia, while the National Anti-Scam Centre has contacted over 10,000 Australians caught up in an international cryptocurrency scam investigation. If you receive unexpected messages claiming to be from myGov, or invoices you don't recognise, do not click any links.

Separately, a new Sydney-based cybersecurity company called Bugtri has launched to help manage the growing flood of AI-generated vulnerability reports hitting businesses. This reflects a broader concern that AI tools are being adopted faster than proper safeguards are put in place.

**Tip:** If you receive a myGov text or email asking you to click a link, go directly to myGov.com.au by typing it into your browser instead.

featured.title: Proofpoint warns of myGov & invoice scams in Australia
featured.quote: Australians lost AUD $2.18 billion to scams in 2025, with fake myGov logins as primary vector.
